scope.stage: Tear size, chronicity and functional loss must be known.
scope.operativeStatus: Nonoperative studies separate from repairs; no generic postoperative regimen.
scope.uncertainty: Symptom improvement does not show tendon healing; long-term structural progression may coexist.

sources.design: Evidence-based guideline with systematic evidence synthesis
sources.population: Small/medium symptomatic full-thickness tears; separate large/massive/unrepairable and postoperative topics.
sources.comparator: Physical therapy versus repair and postoperative management comparisons.
sources.outcomes: Both PT and repair improve patient outcomes; nonoperative tear size/atrophy/fatty infiltration may progress over 5–10 years.
sources.uncertainty: No generic safe workout dose/ROM cap; subgroup heterogeneity.
sources.harms: Structural progression and repair integrity discussed; not an injury incidence for each exercise.
sources.limitations: Early/delayed repair mobilization evidence is not unrestricted resistance clearance.

protocol.execution: Guideline supports selected nonoperative physical therapy; exact individual exercise not standardized.
protocol.progression: Postoperative and tear-size pathways separate; no universal ordinary-training progression.

sources.design: Prospective multicenter cohort; 452 enrolled, follow-up report includes 422
sources.population: Symptomatic MRI-confirmed atraumatic full-thickness tears, age 18–100; injury-related presentation/prior surgery/GHOA/capsulitis excluded.
sources.comparator: No randomized control; surgery election defined failure.
sources.coInterventions: Manual mobilization as needed; heat/cold recommended; education/home materials.
sources.outcomes: Approximately 75% avoided surgery at two years; patient outcomes improved.
sources.uncertainty: Preferences/selection influence surgery; no untreated comparator or proof of healing.
sources.harms: Exercise-specific adverse-event surveillance not clearly reported.
sources.limitations: Not acute traumatic tears, repairs or combined-pathology clearance.

protocol.execution: Daily postural/assisted/active ROM and scapular motion; anterior/posterior shoulder stretches; cuff/scapular strengthening. Exact anterior-stretch setup absent without linked booklet.
protocol.dose: not reported for exact exercise repetitions/hold times in inspected main manuscript.
protocol.supervision: Therapist instruction/books/DVD; transition home when ready.
protocol.progression: Clinical reassessment at six weeks; improve/continue, cured, or no better/surgical discussion.
protocol.stoppingRules: not reported as a numeric exercise-specific stopping rule.

sources.design: Randomized trial fifteen-year follow-up; 103 randomized, 83 assessed
sources.population: Full-thickness tears ≤3 cm; gradual-onset and minor-trauma acute-on-chronic presentations.
sources.comparator: Primary repair versus tailored physiotherapy with optional secondary repair.
sources.coInterventions: Surgical group acromioplasty and sometimes biceps tenodesis.
sources.outcomes: Repair favored Constant by 11.8 and ASES by 13.9 points; 15/51 PT crossed to surgery. In 26 unrepaired tears AP size increased 16.2→31.6 mm.
sources.uncertainty: Small trial, crossover and attrition; not every acute traumatic or massive tear.
sources.harms: Retears after surgery and additional treatments reported; no evidence a particular gym exercise caused enlargement.
sources.limitations: Long-term functional conflict with nonoperative cohort must remain; no universal load cap.

protocol.execution: Individually adapted outpatient physiotherapy, not a single isolated exercise; postoperative repair protocol separate.
protocol.dose: PT 40-min sessions twice weekly first 12 weeks, decreasing following 6–12 weeks.
protocol.progression: Insufficient progress after ≥15 sessions could prompt reassessment/secondary surgery. Repair arm passive ROM immediately, active at six weeks, strength after twelve weeks: trial only.
protocol.stoppingRules: Persistent clinical findings prompted review; no exercise-specific numeric stop threshold.
